title: What is known about 1RB0RA_0LC0RE_1LE1LD_0LE---_1LF0LC_1RA1LE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RA_0LC0RE_1LE1LD_0LE---_1LF0LC_1RA1LE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. Its run is a clock: a block of 1s at the left end grows by two cells per tick, and tick k rewrites the word to the right of the block by applying one fixed map P to it exactly 2k times. P is a single trip of the head into the word and back. This page lists what has been established, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The clock is proved in Lean for every k and every word: if P takes the word through 2k trips, the tick happens, in an exactly known number of steps. What P does to the word over many trips, and what happens when a trip does not come back (the end of a phase), is not proved. An exact accelerated simulator, checked against the direct one at every visit of the left end in the first 2·1010 steps, follows the run through 30 phases to 2.363·10194 steps without a halt.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 264 cells have been visited and 137 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Sweep rules
claims.text: The self-loops of the table cross runs of any length: sweep_A1, for every length and every tape around.

claims.title: Where it can halt
claims.text: The only halting transition is D on 1, and D is entered only from C on 1 (1LD): the machine halts exactly when C reads a 1 whose left neighbour is a 1, 1 C>1. Both directions are proved in Lean, by a case split on the cells the head reads: a configuration halts one step later if and only if it is 1 C>1 (halt_iff_1), so a halting run from blank passes through it (halts_blank_pred_1).

claims.title: The sweep and the merge
claims.text: rule_sweep: 0 0 F> 1^(3+2n) 0 becomes 1 0^(4+2n) 1 B> (the block is swept into 0s); rule_merge: 1 0 F> 1 becomes F> 1 1 1, for every n and all tapes around.

claims.title: The clock, for every k
claims.text: tick: for every k, every word W and all tapes L, if W reaches W' by 2k P-steps (each one an excursion L 0^3 1 B> W → L F> 1^3 0 W') of total cost E, then L 0 0 F> 1^(3+2k) 0 W reaches L F> 1^(3+2k+2) 0 W' in exactly E + 12·2k − 2 steps. Strong induction on k: the tick is the sweep, one P-step, ticks 0 … k−1, and the merge. tick_left_end: the same at the left end of the tape.

claims.title: The exact accelerated run
claims.text: holdouts/1RB0RA_0LC0RE_1LE1LD_0LE---_1LF0LC_1RA1LE/py/clock.py simulates cell by cell, but does a tick at once when its 2k P-steps all come back (the theorem above; P computed by running the machine, P2k memoized on the part of the word it reads). It gives the same time, block and word as tools/c/tmrun.c at every visit of the left end in the first 2·1010 steps, and follows the run through 30 phases to 2.363·10194 steps: no halt.

claims.title: What the word does
claims.text: In the word, read as blocks of 1s, the front is a gadget of period 8 under P, followed by a binary counter whose digits are the 4-cell words 1 0 1 0 (blocks 1 1: digit 0) and 1 1 1 0 (block 3: digit 1), least significant first; every 8 P-steps the counter goes down by one (seen from a phase start: 12, 11, 10, …, 5 at P-steps 8, 16, …, 64). Deeper blocks (5, 7, 9, …) change only when a borrow reaches them. A phase ends when the front reads 1 0 0 or 1 1 0: the counter has run out.

claims.title: What a phase does to the word
claims.text: At almost every phase end from step 2,985 to 10<sup>60</sup> steps the new word has |W| + L + 2 cells (L the last block; exceptions +3, +4, +14), keeping only a short tail of the old word; over a phase the word changes at the front and in a group of cells near its end. No simple phase-to-phase map was found.
claims.where: holdouts/1RB0RA_0LC0RE_1LE1LD_0LE---_1LF0LC_1RA1LE/py/clock.py (Hybrid.visits), comparing the words at the first and last visit of each phase

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: A normal tick cannot halt (the clock theorem). Halting needs a P-step that does not come back — that happens only at the end of a phase — followed by C on a 1 with a 1 to its left (1 C>1). Open: what P does over 2k trips (a counter in the word), what a phase end builds, and whether one ever reaches the halting configuration.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows whether it halts. Started on a blank tape, this machine runs a clock: a block of 1s at the left end grows by two cells per tick, and tick k applies one map P to the word beside the block 2<sup>k</sup> times. The clock is proved in Lean for every tick whose 2<sup>k</sup> trips all return; an exact accelerated run follows it through 30 phases to 2.363·10<sup>194</sup> steps.

facts.text: Whenever its 2<sup>k</sup> trips all return, tick k = 2<sup>k</sup> trips P of the head into the word, in E + 12·2<sup>k</sup> − 2 steps.
No halt, in an exact accelerated run through 30 phases.
Halting needs a trip that does not come back and then C on a 1 with a 1 to its left (1 C>1).

sections.heading: A block that grows by two, each tick twice as long
html: Watch the tape each time the head, in state E, sits at the left end. It always reads E>0 1^L 0 W: a block of L ones, then a word W of short blocks. Within a phase L grows by 2 per visit and each visit takes about twice as long as the one before. From the real run:

Inside one tick the machine runs a recursion. The head sweeps the block into 0s, makes one trip into the word W (a P-step: it rewrites the front of W and comes back), and then performs ticks 0, 1, …, k−1 on a new small block, each one eating two of the 0s it left; finally it merges. So tick k contains one P-step plus ticks 0 … k−1: 1 + 1 + 2 + … + 2k−1 = 2k P-steps in all. The word sees nothing but P, applied 2k times.

This is proved in Lean for every k and every word (tick in lean/Clock.lean): if 2k P-steps of total cost E take W to W', then 0 0 F> 1^(3+2k) 0 W reaches F> 1^(3+2k+2) 0 W' in exactly E + 12·2k − 2 steps.

sections.heading: What P does to the word
html: Read the word as blocks of 1s separated by 0s. From the visit at step 198,027 (block 1^3), applying P again and again (each line one P-step):

The front (left of the bar) runs through a cycle of 8 words. Behind it is a binary counter: digit 0 is the pair of blocks 1 1, digit 1 is a block 3 (both four cells with their 0s), least significant digit first. Every 8 P-steps the counter goes down by one: after 8, 16, 24, …, 64 P-steps it reads 12, 11, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5. So P is, in effect, a decrement, and a tick k subtracts 2k. When the counter runs out the front reads 1 0 0 or 1 1 0 and the next trip does not come back.

sections.heading: A phase ends when a trip does not come back
html: The tick needs every one of its 2k trips to come back to the block. When one does not (the front of the word has run out), the clock breaks: the head goes on to the left over the half-built recursion, the block is dissolved into the word, and a new phase starts from a short block. sections.heading: What halting would take
html: The only halting transition is D on 1, and D is entered only from C on 1 (1LD): the machine halts exactly when C reads a 1 whose left neighbour is a 1, 1 C>1.

A normal tick never halts: the Lean theorem says it reaches its end. So a halt can only come at the end of a phase, in the trip that does not come back or in what follows it before the next visit of the left end. The accelerated run simulates exactly those parts cell by cell, and none of the 30 phase ends halted. Whether a later one does depends on the word the earlier phases built, which looks irregular: the question is open.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

family: clock and word map (block grows by 2, the word is rewritten by 2^k excursions)
summary: A clock: at each visit of the left end in state E the block 1^(3+2k) has grown by 2, and the word to its right has gone through 2^k applications of one map P (one excursion of the head into the word) — proved in Lean for every k, for each tick whose 2^k trips all return; a phase ends when P fails to come back. Exact accelerated run: 30 phases to 2.363·10<sup>194</sup> steps, no halt. Halting needs C on a 1 with a 1 to its left (1 C>1).
